dovish.title: Job Openings Edge Lower
dovish.summary: JOLTS openings fell to 7.271M, slightly below forecast and the prior month.
dovish.source: BLS JOLTS via FXStreet / TradingEconomics calendar
dovish.reason: Openings declined 88k from the prior month and undershot consensus by 29k. The miss is modest, so it adds a 1.0 dovish labour-demand signal rather than displacing Friday payrolls as the main catalyst.

dovish.title: ADP Employment Misses Before Payrolls
dovish.summary: Private payroll growth slowed to 38k, below the 47k forecast.
dovish.reason: The modest private-payroll miss reinforces JOLTS cooling ahead of Friday NFP, but it is too small to overwhelm sticky prices or the hawkish Fed-futures strip.

hawkish.title: Hawkish 3-Vote Dissent at July FOMC
hawkish.summary: Three regional Fed presidents wanted a hike at the last meeting — the Committee is split.
hawkish.reason: Re-verified 2026-08-28 via federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260729a.htm: 9-3 hold with Hammack, Kashkari, Logan preferring +25bp. Warsh's Aug 28 speech ('predominant focus on prices', 'otherwise we have work to do') moved the Chair rhetorically toward the dissenters — the hawkish cluster is no longer isolated.

hawkish.title: Warsh Jackson Hole: 'Predominant Focus on Prices'
hawkish.summary: Fed Chair Warsh: inflation is the predominant focus — no cut pre-commitment, 'otherwise we have work to do'.
hawkish.source: Federal Reserve — Chair Warsh, 'In Our Time', Jackson Hole

data.previous: July stmt: solid growth, elevated uncertainty

hawkish.reason: Warsh said the Fed's predominant focus should be on prices, described labour as consistent with full employment and financial conditions as hard to call restrictive, and said he was committed to a discipline rather than a decision. Current pricing is shown only in meetings.fed.pricing.

hawkish.title: Long-End Yields Remain Above 4.75% Trigger
hawkish.summary: The 10Y closed Sep 9 above the desk 4.75% trigger; this is market context, not proof of Fed causation.
hawkish.reason: Current Sep 9 closes keep the desk long-end threshold breached. This is contemporaneous financial-conditions context only; no causal attribution to one release.

hawkish.title: ISM Services and Prices Reaccelerate
hawkish.summary: Services activity beat expectations and prices paid accelerated, strengthening the Fed hawks.
hawkish.reason: The headline beat and acceleration in prices paid and new orders validate sticky services inflation ahead of the Sep FOMC. Employment remained below 50, so the signal is strong but capped at 2.0 rather than 2.5.

hawkish.title: Payrolls Rebound Far Above Forecast
hawkish.summary: August payrolls jumped 162k versus 56k expected while unemployment held at 4.1%.
hawkish.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics · Employment Situation
hawkish.reason: The last payroll report before Sep FOMC decisively reversed July weakness. A 106k consensus beat, steady 4.1% unemployment and a small wage beat raise the hurdle for a cut; ZQU26 fell 1.0bp from Sep 3 and the desk hike proxy rose from 49% to 56%. Weight capped at 2.0 because the inflation releases still decide hold versus hike.

hawkish.title: Producer Inflation Remains Hot
hawkish.summary: August headline PPI met a hot 0.4% monthly forecast and accelerated to 5.4% y/y; core monthly PPI undershot.
hawkish.source: TradingEconomics calendar (BLS static page inaccessible this run)

data.actual: headline +0.4% MoM / +5.4% YoY; core +0.2% MoM / +4.6% YoY
data.previous: headline +0.1% revised / +4.8% revised; core +0.3% revised / +4.3% revised
data.delta_label: headline YoY beat +0.1pp; core MoM miss -0.1pp

hawkish.reason: Headline producer inflation stayed elevated and the yearly rate exceeded consensus, supporting the hawkish side before CPI. The softer core monthly print makes the release mixed, so weight is capped at 1.5. Actual, consensus and revised previous values were observed in the Sep 10 TradingEconomics calendar; BLS was inaccessible from this host.

dovish.title: Canada Employment Contracts as Wage Growth Slows
dovish.summary: Canada lost 41.7k jobs versus a 15k gain expected; wage growth slowed to 2.0%.
dovish.source: Statistics Canada · Labour Force Survey, August 2026
dovish.reason: Employment fell 41.7k against a 15k gain expected and wage growth slowed to 2.0% from 2.8%, a material demand-and-inflation cooling signal after the Sep 2 hold. Unemployment did not rise, limiting weight to 2.0.

dovish.title: Asking-Rent Inflation Turns Negative
dovish.summary: Two-bedroom asking rents across Canadian CMAs fell 3.6% y/y, a secondary shelter-disinflation signal.
dovish.source: Statistics Canada · Quarterly rent statistics, Q2 2026
dovish.reason: The experimental all-CMA two-bedroom asking-rent measure fell 3.6% year over year, versus -0.9% in the prior quarterly release. This is a secondary BoC dovish shelter signal, not a quality-adjusted CPI rent measure and not evidence of immediate policy repricing.

hawkish.title: WTI Energy Pressure Extends Intraday Sep 10
hawkish.summary: WTI traded at 101.95 intraday, extending Canada energy and gasoline inflation pressure.
hawkish.source: Yahoo Finance CL=F daily structured price
hawkish.reason: WTI extended its multi-session rise in the Sep 10 open session. This mutable intraday quote is current energy/terms-of-trade and gasoline-inflation context, not a final settlement and not an attributed reaction to one BoC event.

hawkish.title: CAD GDP Beat — Sep 2 Hold Now Base Case
hawkish.summary: Q2 GDP +0.8% QoQ led by exports; June +0.3% MoM beat — the make-or-break print broke hawkish.

data.delta_label: MoM beat +0.1; ann. -0.1 vs fcst but rebound from -0.1

hawkish.reason: StatCan verified 2026-08-28: Q2 real GDP +0.8% QoQ (~3.3% annualized), Q1 revised 0.0 -> +0.1%, led by exports, household spending and business investment. The pre-decision make-or-break printed strong — The GDP rebound was validated by the Sep 2 hold at 2.25%. Weight raised 1.5 -> 2.0 as the decisive domestic data point.

hawkish.title: BoC Holds 2.25% and Flags Energy/Tariff Inflation
hawkish.summary: The BoC held at 2.25% as high oil and tariffs kept inflation risks alive.
hawkish.reason: The decision matched consensus, but the official statement emphasized high energy prices, tariffs, tighter financial conditions and CPI near 3%. No market-reaction attribution is made without a frozen event-window price set.

hawkish.title: Ivey PMI Surges After BoC Hold
hawkish.summary: Canada Ivey PMI jumped to 64.3 versus 56.2 expected, offsetting part of the jobs shock.
hawkish.reason: The broad activity gauge accelerated sharply two days after the BoC hold, arguing against an immediate growth-collapse response. It is a meaningful counterweight to weak employment, but a survey cannot outweigh the official labour report, so weight is 1.5.
